I am bringing back the Stoicism quote series I did last year. Today is one from Epictetus who is possibly the most influential of all Stoics.

God has entrusted me with myself. No man is free who is not master of himself.

–Epictetus

This is a fairly simple quote, but it has a lot of depth to it. It just all depends on your interpretation. Feel free to post your thoughts below.

This is an interesting one to me. It can be interpreted in the most literal sense of not being a slave, but I think it is much more than that personally. To me it is more about controlling yourself and your actions/emotions. You cannot control what happens to you, you can only control how you respond. By being under control at all times, you are the master of yourself. If you give in to anger or allow yourself to be goaded, you are giving control of yourself to someone or something else.

Not "how you respond"... the quote to me is a template for proactive living versus the pitfalls of reactivity. Mind over matter/circumstances... the anchor is mastery over your "perceived" present circumstances.
That is certainly a valid interpretation. From what I've read about stoicism (which isn't much, but it's been valuable), I believe both meanings are correct and that Epictetus fully meant both.
I do though find that stoicism is a solid base foundation and largely assistive. Glad you're gonna go back to the daily... refreshers are good.

"...a wicked man, though a king, is a slave. For he serves, not one man alone, but what is worse, as many masters as he has vices." - St. Augustine

Stoicism often gets taken for granted because people have very crude, sort of aphoristic assumptions about what Stoicism is. They are often conflating Stoicism with their understanding of the use of the word 'stoic', as in "He was very stoic." Granted, they are related, but Stoicism is a sophisticated philosophical system, possibly one of the more sophisticated and practical philosophies from the classic period. It's so much more than "keep a stiff upper lip, boy".
